<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - This is an open-source monorepo for the “TanStack Query” library, a set of framework-agnostic data-fetching, caching, and updating hooks.  
   - It provides a core engine plus adapters for React, Solid, Svelte, Vue, Angular, persisters, devtools, codemods, and examples/integrations.

2. Analyze the file structure  
   - Top-level configuration: pnpm-workspace, nx.json, tsconfig.json, scripts, docs, examples, integrations.  
   - The packages/ directory contains many sub-packages, each with its own src/, tests/, tsconfig.json, build configs (tsup.config.js or vite.config.ts).  
   - Key packages:  
     • query-core (the engine)  
     • react-query, solid-query, svelte-query, vue-query, angular-query-experimental, etc. (framework adapters)  
     • query-devtools, react-query-devtools, solid-query-devtools, vue-query-devtools, svelte-query-devtools (devtools)  
     • query-persist-client-core, react-query-persist-client, solid-query-persist-client, query-async-storage-persister, query-sync-storage-persister (persistence layers)  
     • query-codemods (migration scripts)  
   - Examples/ showcases usage in multiple frameworks and integrations/ demonstrates embedding in various toolchains.

3. Examine README for additional insights  
   - The README highlights the core features (auto caching, stale-while-revalidate, mutations, pagination, infinite scroll, suspense, devtools).  
   - It positions TanStack Query as transport-agnostic and multi-framework.

4. Components of the system design diagram  
   a. Main components  
      • Core Engine (query-core)  
      • Framework Adapters: React, Vue, Solid, Svelte, Angular  
      • Persistence Layer(s)  
      • Devtools Layer(s)  
      • Codemods (migration tools)  
      • Examples & Integrations (consumers)  
   b. Relationships and interactions  
      • Arrows from Core → each Adapter (they import and wrap core APIs)  
      • Adapters → Persistence Layer (optional plug-in relationship)  
      • Adapters → Devtools Layer (hook registration for devtools)  
      • Codemods → Adapters/Core (transform code for upgrades)  
      • Examples/Integrations → Adapters/Core (demonstrate usage)  
   c. Architectural patterns and design principles  
      • Monorepo Workspace (shared build/config scripts, consistent linting, testing)  
      • Plugin/Adapter pattern: core engine defines interfaces, adapters bind to framework lifecycles.  
      • Layered architecture: Core → Adapters → Application (examples)  
      • Dependency injection via providers (ReactQueryClientProvider, QueryClientProvider in Svelte, etc.)  
   d. Relevant technologies  
      • TypeScript, Vite, tsup, Nx/PNPM workspace  
      • Testing frameworks (vitest, Jest variants)  
      • Build tools (tsup, vite)  

5. Guidelines for an open-source tool diagram  
   - Emphasize the core engine as the heart of the system  
   - Show adapters as extension points — draw them in a ring around core  
   - Highlight persisters and devtools as optional plug-ins (use dotted arrows)  
   - Show examples/integrations at the perimeter as end-users of adapters  

6. Diagramming elements to include  
   - Clear labels: “Core Engine”, “React Adapter”, “Vue Adapter”, “Devtools”, “Persistence”  
   - Directional arrows for “depends on” or “extends” relationships  
   - Color coding or shape variations:  
     • Core in one color (e.g., blue rectangle)  
     • Adapters in another (e.g., green circles)  
     • Devtools/Persisters in a third (e.g., orange hexagons)  
     • Examples/Integrations in a fourth (e.g., grey parallelograms)  
   - Space out the layers with extra vertical or horizontal gaps so that arrows do not overlap  
     • Add more space between the core, adapter ring, and outer consumer ring so that connecting arrows are more visible.  

7. Step-by-step drawing approach  
   1) Draw a central box labeled “query-core (Core Engine)”  
   2) Around it, draw one shape per framework adapter, each connected to the core with a thick arrow  
   3) Off each adapter, draw optional persister and devtools shapes, connected with dotted arrows  
   4) On the outermost layer, draw example apps and integration toolchains, each pointing inward to the adapter they use  
   5) Annotate major flows:  
       • Data request flow from app → adapter → core → network  
       • Cache invalidation flow core → adapter → app  
       • Devtools hook registration flow adapter → devtools  
   6) Use generous spacing between each layer (core-adapter-plugin-consumer) so arrows remain clear  

By following this tailored layout, you’ll capture the essential architecture of TanStack Query: a single core engine, layered adapters, extensibility via plugins, and consumer examples—all clearly labeled, spaced, and color-coded for maximum clarity.  
</explanation>
